query: How can clinics improve triage and scheduling?

per_column.name: clinical_acuity_level
per_column.rationale: Clinical acuity is an intrinsic patient/case attribute, not a lever a clinic can set. It plausibly drives both how a case is triaged/scheduled and its efficiency, so it functions as a confounder rather than an intervenable treatment. Related to but richer than the existing 'urgency' column.

per_column.name: visit_type_category
per_column.rationale: Type of visit (acute vs chronic vs preventive) is a case characteristic, not something the clinic decides. It affects triage priority and scheduling load, acting as a common cause / case-mix confounder.

per_column.name: complexity_driver
per_column.rationale: Underlying complexity of the presenting problem is an intrinsic case property affecting both routing and efficiency; a case-mix confounder, not an intervenable lever.

per_column.name: required_diagnostic_workup
per_column.rationale: Whether imaging/labs are ordered lies on the pathway between the case and its scheduling/throughput outcome. It is a downstream step of the triage process, so it behaves as a mediator rather than a confounder or a settable treatment.

per_column.name: specialty_routing_signal
per_column.rationale: Routing/escalation/referral is itself part of the triage-and-scheduling process, sitting between case characteristics and efficiency, hence a mediator.

per_column.name: care_continuity_type
per_column.rationale: New vs established/follow-up status is a case attribute that influences both scheduling pathway and efficiency; a common-cause confounder, not a clinic-settable lever.

per_column.name: in_visit_procedure_performed
per_column.rationale: A procedure performed during the visit is a downstream event on the visit-processing pathway, affecting duration/throughput; treated as a mediator, not a pre-treatment confounder.

per_column.name: pediatric_age_vulnerability
per_column.rationale: Derived from age_group; an immutable patient attribute that can influence triage priority and scheduling. Confounder, not intervenable.

judge.rationale: The query asks a genuinely interventional what-if question ('how can clinics improve triage and scheduling') where the actor is the clinic and the outcome is scheduling/triage efficiency. To satisfy the technical claim, the added columns needed at least one INTERVENABLE treatment lever the clinic could set (e.g., staffing level, appointment-slot policy, triage protocol assignment, walk-in vs pre-booked, provider allocation) plus confounders. However, NONE of the added columns is a settable lever: every column is either an intrinsic case/patient attribute (acuity, visit type, complexity, continuity, pediatric vulnerability) or a downstream process step (diagnostic workup, routing signal, in-visit procedure). The intrinsic attributes are case-mix confounders and the process steps are mediators. Because there is no intervenable treatment, the interventional what-if setup fails despite the presence of several plausible, not-named-in-query confounders.
